topic: Multi-user API proxy with JWT authentication and rate limiting
chosen_direction: Simple REST proxy with JWT auth, PostgreSQL user management, Redis rate limiting, full observability from day 1

requirements_summary.WHO: Multiple users accessing shared proxy; maintained by you (selfhost)
requirements_summary.WHAT: Proxy server forwarding requests to https://vip.digishop.work/v1 with JWT auth + auto-retry
requirements_summary.WHEN: No specific deadline; production-ready from day 1
requirements_summary.WHY: Share single API key with multiple users securely
requirements_summary.HOW: JWT authentication, auto-retry on failure, Node.js + Express, PostgreSQL user storage

db_design_options.name: PostgreSQL with Minimal Schema
db_design_options.schema_notes: Normalized (3NF) with users + request_logs tables. UUID primary keys, indexes on username/email.

db_design_options.name: MongoDB Document Store
db_design_options.schema_notes: Denormalized documents with embedded request logs (last 100)

db_design_options.name: SQLite with File Storage
db_design_options.schema_notes: Same schema as PostgreSQL but file-based

api_contract_draft.user_rationale: Simple REST proxy chosen for transparency and ease of use. Users just replace base URL.

risk_matrix.mitigation: Implement key redaction in all logs. Never log raw API key. Use structured logging with sanitization. Test log output before deploy.
Implement per-user rate limiting (Redis-backed). Add global rate limit as fallback. Monitor API usage daily. Set up cost alerts.
Use strong random secret (256-bit min). Store in env var only. Document secret rotation procedure. Implement rotation before launch.
Configure connection pool (max 20). Add health check monitoring. Set up alerts for connection count > 15. Test under load.
Implement SIGTERM handler with 30s timeout. Test Docker stop behavior. Add pre-shutdown health check.

security: JWT Secret Management: Use strong random JWT secret (min 256-bit), store in env var, rotate periodically
API Key Exposure in Logs: Never log the actual API key. Redact in request_logs. Use separate audit logs with restricted access
Rate Limiting Bypass: Implement per-user rate limiting (100 req/hour) + global rate limiting. Use Redis for distributed counters
devops: Database Connection Pool Exhaustion: Use pg with connection pool (max 20). Add health check. Monitor active connections
No Graceful Shutdown: Implement SIGTERM handler with 30s timeout. Close DB pool properly
Missing Observability: Add structured logging (Winston/Pino), Prometheus metrics, health check endpoint
end_user: Unclear Error Messages: Return clear error responses with proper HTTP status codes (401, 429, 502, 503)
No Usage Visibility: Add GET /v1/usage endpoint. Include rate limit headers in responses
Registration Flow Unclear: Document registration flow. Add GET /v1/auth/info endpoint
yagni: Request Logs Table Might Be Overkill: Start without request logs. Use stdout logs. Add DB logging only if needed
Refresh Token Pattern Too Complex: Single JWT with 24-hour expiry simpler than access+refresh tokens
Prometheus Metrics Premature: Start with basic health check + structured logs. Add Prometheus when needed
competitor: Industry Pattern: OpenAI-Compatible Proxies: Consider adding OpenAI-compatible endpoints for easier adoption
Existing Solution: Cloudflare Workers AI Gateway: Evaluate before building custom. Self-hosted justified if need full control
Standard Pattern: API Key Rotation: Plan for key rotation from day 1. Store in env var. Document rotation procedure

contradictions_resolved.rationale: Simpler for small user base, can add expiry later if needed
Production-ready from start, easier to debug issues

acceptance_criteria: All HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) forwarded correctly
JWT authentication working (register, login, token validation)
Rate limiting enforced per-user (100 req/hour) and globally (1000 req/hour)
Clear error messages with proper HTTP status codes
API key never exposed in logs
architecture_decisions: Node.js + Express for proxy server (simple, widely understood)
PostgreSQL for user management (production-ready, easy to scale)
JWT with no expiry (user choice for simplicity)
Connection pooling (max 20) to prevent DB exhaustion
test_strategy: Unit tests: auth, rate limiting, key redaction. Integration tests: mock target API, full request flow. Load tests: verify rate limiting + connection pooling. Security tests: JWT tampering, key exposure in logs. E2E tests: Docker Compose stack, full deployment.
